newsitem.title: USA: Mountain lion kills boy at Rocky Mountain park.
newsitem.headline: Mountain lion kills boy at Rocky Mountain park.

text.p: A mountain lion killed a 10-year-old boy walking along a popular hiking trail in Rocky Mountain National Park, the first fatal attack by wildlife in the park's history, officials said on Friday.
Park officials later killed the 88-pound apparently healthy female mountain lion.

Mark David Miedema of Lakewood, Colorado, had walked ahead of his parents and 6-year-old sister on Thursday. They did not see the attack but a few minutes later came upon the boy lying on the trail with his head in the lion's mouth, park spokesman Doug Caldwall said.
The lion was chased away, but the boy had suffered bite wounds to his head and could not be revived.
It was the first fatal attack by an animal since the popular park in Colorado was created in 1915. Two attacks by mountain lions in recent years resulted in injuries.
Last week a mountain lion injured a 4-year-old boy in southwestern Colorado.
Caldwell said visitors were being told not to panic, but to be mindful of wildlife. "This is an area that preserves wildlife. We are not a petting zoo. We are not a theme park," he said.
Caldwell said people facing a mountain lion attack should stand their ground because running triggers an animal's hunting instincts.

People are also advised to make themselves look as big as possible when facing an attack by a mountain lion and to become aggressive. "Stand your ground. Don't lose eye contact. Make yourself look bigger," Caldwell said.
